questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Roots of a Transformed Radical Function With an Even Index
questions.worked_solution:
To find the root of $f(x),$  we must solve $f(x)=0:$

$$
-5\sqrt[4]{3x+1}+10=0
$$

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-5\sqrt[4]{3x+1}+10 & =0 \\ -5\sqrt[4]{3x+1} & =-10 \\ \sqrt[4]{3x+1} & =2 \\ (\sqrt[4]{3x+1})^{4} & ={2}^{4} \\ 3x+1 & =16 \\ 3x & =15 \\ x & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we must check the answer by substituting it back into the initial equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}-5\sqrt[4]{3\cdot 5+1}+10 & =0 \\ -5\sqrt[4]{16}+10 & =0 \\ -5\cdot 2+10 & =0 \\ 0 & =0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the root of $f(x)$ is $x=5.$

questions.worked_solution:
To find the root of $f(x),$  we must solve $f(x)=0:$

$$
-4\sqrt[6]{5x-11}-8=0
$$

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-4\sqrt[6]{5x-11}-8 & =0 \\ -4\sqrt[6]{5x-11} & =8 \\ \sqrt[6]{5x-11} & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

This equation does not have any solutions since its left-hand side is always nonnegative, while the right-hand side is negative.

Therefore, $f(x)$ has no root.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Roots of a Transformed Radical Function With an Odd Index
questions.worked_solution:
To find the root of $f(x),$ we must solve $f(x)=0:$

$$
2\sqrt[5]{7-6x}+6=0
$$

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\sqrt[5]{7-6x}+6 & =0 \\ 2\sqrt[5]{7-6x} & =-6 \\ \sqrt[5]{7-6x} & =-3 \\ (\sqrt[5]{7-6x})^{5} & =(-3)^{5} \\ 7-6x & =-243 \\ -6x & =-250 \\ x & =\frac{125}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the root of $f(x)$ is $x=\frac{125}{3}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Roots of a Transformed Radical Function With an Odd Index
questions.worked_solution:
To find the root of $f(x),$ we must solve $f(x)=0:$

$$
9\sqrt[7]{2x-6}-9=0
$$

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9\sqrt[7]{2x-6}-9 & =0 \\ 9\sqrt[7]{2x-6} & =9 \\ \sqrt[7]{2x-6} & =1 \\ (\sqrt[7]{2x-6})^{7} & ={1}^{7} \\ 2x-6 & =1 \\ 2x & =7 \\ x & =\frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the root of $f(x)$ is $x=\frac{7}{2}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Roots of a Transformed Radical Function With an Even Index
questions.worked_solution:
To find the roots of $f(x),$ we must solve $f(x)=0:$

$$
-5\sqrt[8]{4x+9}+5=0
$$

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-5\sqrt[8]{4x+9}+5 & =0 \\ -5\sqrt[8]{4x+9} & =-5 \\ \sqrt[8]{4x+9} & =1 \\ {(\sqrt[8]{4x+9})}^{8} & ={1}^{8} \\ 4x+9 & =1 \\ 4x & =-8 \\ x & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we must check the answer by substituting it back into the initial equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}-5\sqrt[8]{4\cdot (-2)+9}+5 & =0 \\ -5\sqrt[8]{1}+5 & =0 \\ -5\cdot 1+5 & =0 \\ 0 & =0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the root of $f(x)$ is $x=-2.$
